performance_case.causal_mechanism: Abnormal trading activity may contain decision-time information about participation, attention, liquidity demand, or informed order flow, but raw volume may instead be contemporaneous reaction to returns and may fail out of sample. A useful incremental mechanism must condition or transform volume in a way distinct from the frozen prior-20-day median ratio.
performance_case.claim_boundary: This task may use only the five frozen primary publisher pages to produce one preregistration-ready idea skeleton or close the volume discovery family. It cannot inspect any historical or forward strategy outcome, prove exact BTC predictability, PnL, drawdown, fees, fills, slippage, capacity, candidate readiness, or OOS value; it cannot change the existing volume screen or register, execute, deploy, or activate anything.
performance_case.drawdown_hypothesis: Only a later matched-capital experiment could test whether an incremental decision-time volume mechanism filters adverse entry paths and reduces maximum drawdown. This literature-only task has zero immediate drawdown effect and leaves the direction and magnitude MISSING_PROOF.
performance_case.opportunity_cost: A narrow primary-source screen can avoid spending scarce forward evidence and runner time on a raw-volume idea already contradicted out of sample, while the one-idea cap prevents literature search from displacing direct evidence-ready work or expanding into unbounded factor mining.
performance_case.performance_hypothesis: If a literature-supported volume transformation is observable before entry, independent of the frozen raw-volume ratio, and later survives frozen equal-capital fee and path-risk gates, it may improve fee-adjusted total PnL by rejecting low-information DRA entries. The present task makes no performance claim.
